headlines.description: The government’s central witness in the federal corruption trial for former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao was grilled by the defense Friday morning. The defense was trying to impeach the credibility of businessman Mario Juarez, who already has pleaded guilty to one crime in connection with the alleged bribery and corruption scheme involving Thao. Juarez agreed to testify on behalf of the government in hopes for a lighter sentence. Federal prosecutors claim David and Andy Duong, who own California Waste Solutions, and Evolutionary Homes, which was co-founded with Juarez, conspired with Thao and her longtime partner Andre Jones to use her political power in exchange for business favors and money for Jones. During trial Friday, one defense attorney questioned Juarez about the fairness of the plea deal given that Juarez has only been charged with one count of conspiracy while his alleged co-conspirators face several charges. “I pled to the crime I was guilty of,” Juarez said on the stand Friday. “You didn’t have to plead to bribery, right?” David Duong’s attorney asked. “I bribed Mayor Sheng Thao,” Juarez said. “We all committed bribery.” “You didn’t have to plea to it,” the attorney said. “You are correct,” Juarez responded. The defense attorney questioned Juarez about back-and-forth emails between him and his attorneys as they tried to hash out the plea agreement – emails that lost attorney-client privilege because Juarez forwarded them to a friend. In those exchanges, Juarez threatened to pull his cooperation if the government didn’t pursue charges against the defendants. “Do you think I’m playing with fire?” Juarez emailed to his friend. The attorney for David Duong questioned whether Juarez was truthful with the FBI when describing how he allegedly defrauded the printing company behind the negative mailers that helped get Thao elected mayor. “You’re misunderstanding and misconstruing information,” Juarez said on the stand. “Or are you just not listening or you just want to hear something different?” he said moments later. Oakland Nov 5 Sheng Thao Oct 30 Sheng Thao Oct 29 Former Oakland city employees testify in Sheng Thao corruption trial
